findings.claim: The launcher and npm-generated global shim select different binaries when both x64 and arm64 executables exist on Windows ARM64.
findings.evidence: Run 33002500967: base and head both-present launcher cells both select arm64. The real npm-installed .cmd selects x64 while both 12,548,608-byte arm64 and 13,642,752-byte x64 files exist. The divergence is real and end-to-end, but the base cell proves it predates this diff. The prior review incorrectly inferred novelty from base's x64-only hard error, which has the opposite precondition.
findings.layer: installed package and entry-point dispatch on Windows ARM64

findings.claim: When neither executable exists on Windows ARM64, the head error names win32-arm64 and then says it expected agent-browser-win32-x64.exe.
findings.evidence: Run 33002500967 head job 98287683210 forced the neither-present state: exit 1 and Expected ...win32-x64.exe while the preceding error says No binary found for win32-arm64. Base job 98287683496 expected ...win32-arm64.exe, proving the inconsistency is introduced by this diff. Fix by naming the resolved fallback explicitly or making both lines use one architecture model.

findings.claim: The PR's committed launcher suite omits the neither-present failure cell, does not exercise the global-shim entry point, and fabricates executable files instead of invoking a first-party producer.
findings.evidence: test/launcher.test.mjs has x64-only, both, arm64-only, and Darwin cells, but no neither-present cell and no npm shim drive. Lines 37-46 write marker stubs. The external corpus closes the review gate's proof obligation and confirms why these omitted cells matter, but it does not strengthen the PR's committed regression protection. The real producer was exercised externally, so the producer claim itself is verified; the remaining finding is about what the PR will protect after merge.

findings.evidence: The suite imports only Node builtins and devDependencies is empty. The workflow's dependency-free version-sync sibling invokes node directly; jobs that set up pnpm also install dependencies. Using pnpm keeps the package script single-sourced, so this is nit-tier.

findings.claim: The source-built native Windows ARM64 binary panics when running agent-browser install.
findings.evidence: Run 33002500967 job 98287683603: the COFF 0xAA64 binary exited 101 and panicked at cli/src/install.rs:181 with Unsupported platform for Chrome for Testing download. run_install guards Linux aarch64 only, while platform_key has no Windows aarch64 case. The x64 image under emulation proceeded to Downloading Chrome 152.0.7977.64 for win64. This defect predates the PR, but it means the binary the new launcher prefers cannot perform install while the fallback it deprioritizes can.
